— a draft and its published parent collapse to one logical node so the graph never shows a ghost twin. This keeps the Content Edges Table clean: edges are drawn between published identities, mined by the Edge Extractor from published Reference Field values.

, not reuse the published edges. Draft content can add, remove, or repoint references that don't exist in the published version, so a drafts graph that merely reused the published Content Edges Table would lie. Honouring this is what lets editors preview the Blast Radius of a change *before* publishing — the drafts Perspective runs its own extraction pass over draft Reference Field values.

The Perspective is one of the read-time selectors catalogued under API and Contracts: it layers on top of every Dataset read over the HTTP API v1, affects what Postgres Search returns, and is announced through the Capabilities Manifest. The Web Demo and LiveView Studio both let you toggle it. A Document's body — held as a PortableDoc — is itself resolved through the active Perspective, so a draft block tree and its published version never bleed into one another.
